models.deep.general.node module¶

Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODE).

This module implements a Neural ODE model, where the derivative of the hidden state is parameterized by a neural network: dh/dt = f(h, t).

class models.deep.general.node.NeuralODE(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 64, output_dim: int = 1, num_layers: int = 2, time_steps: int = 10, horizon: float = 1.0, output_type: str = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Neural Ordinary Differential Equation Model.

The model predicts the evolution of a state ‘z’ over time: dz/dt = f(z, t, theta)

where f is a neural network.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Dimension of the state z.

  • hidden_dim – Hidden dimension of the derivative network.

  • output_dim – Output dimension (can be different if we project at the end).

  • time_steps – Number of time steps to simulate (default 10).

  • horizon – Time horizon (default 1.0).

forward(x: Tensor, t: Tensor | None = None) → Tensor[source]¶

Forward pass.

Parameters:

  • x – Initial state (batch_size, input_dim).

  • t – Time points (num_steps,). Defaults to linspace(0, horizon, time_steps).

Returns:

trajectory or prediction.

models.deep.general.node.odesolve(func: Callable[[float, Tensor], Tensor], y0: Tensor, t: Tensor, method: str = 'rk4') → Tensor[source]¶

Solve an initial value problem (IVP) using a fixed-step solver.

Parameters:

  • func – Function f(t, y) returning dy/dt.

  • y0 – Initial state (batch_size, state_dim).

  • t – Time points to evaluate at (num_steps,). Must be increasing.

  • method – Solver method (‘rk4’ or ‘euler’).

Returns:

Solution trajectory (num_steps, batch_size, state_dim).

Return type:

y

models.deep.general.pinn module¶

Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN).

This module implements a PINN architecture, which is essentially an MLP that is designed to compute gradients with respect to its inputs (space/time) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs).

class models.deep.general.pinn.PINN(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 20, output_dim: int = 1, num_layers: int = 4, activation: str = 'tanh', output_type: str = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Physics-Informed Neural Network.

A fully connected network that approximates a solution u(x, t) to a PDE. Includes methods to easily compute derivatives du/dx, du/dt, d^2u/dx^2, etc.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Dimension of domain (e.g., 2 for x and t).

  • hidden_dim – Number of neurons per layer.

  • output_dim – Dimension of solution u (e.g., 1 for scalar field).

  • num_layers – Number of hidden layers.

  • activation – Activation function (tanh is standard for PINNs due to smoothness).

forward(x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Forward pass.

Parameters:

x – Collocation points (batch_size, input_dim). Requires requires_grad=True if computing physics loss outside.

gradient(u: Tensor, x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Compute gradient du/dx.

Parameters:

  • u – Output tensor (batch_size, output_dim).

  • x – Input tensor (batch_size, input_dim).

Returns:

Gradient tensor (batch_size, input_dim).

Return type:

grad

laplacian(u: Tensor, x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Compute Laplacian (sum of second derivatives). Note: This is expensive (O(d^2) or O(d) depending on implementation). For input_dim=1 (time), it is just d^2u/dt^2.

models.deep.general.pinn.pinn_loss(u_pred: Tensor, u_target: Tensor | None, f_pred: Tensor, data_weight: float = 1.0, physics_weight: float = 1.0) → dict[str, Tensor][source]¶

Compute PINN loss = MSE_data + MSE_physics.

Parameters:

  • u_pred – Predicted solution at data points.

  • u_target – Target solution (boundary/initial conditions or observed data). Can be None if solving purely unsupervised (unlikely).

  • f_pred – Physics residual at collocation points. Should be close to 0.

Module contents¶

General Neural Architectures.

Standard and specialized neural network components: - Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) - Simple Perceptron - Radial Basis Function Networks (RBF) - Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) - Neural ODEs (Ordinary Differential Equations) - Extreme Learning Machines (ELM)
